stories.summary: The Marsiling Tunnels — home to the only known surviving pre-World War II underground fuel storage tanks in Singapore and the region — will undergo a heritage and archaeological study by the SLA, NHB and URA, due in the first half of 2028, with no firm plans for the 12.5ha site yet.
stories.title: Secluded wartime underground fuel storage tanks in Marsiling to undergo study
stories.why: A forgotten wartime site gets a future — and the study will decide what happens to a rare piece of Singapore's military heritage.

stories.summary: IMDA is investigating Simba over alleged unauthorised spectrum use, and CNA Explains what enforcement action could mean for customers — including possible disruption to their service and mobile numbers.
stories.title: CNA Explains: What could happen to Simba customers if IMDA takes action against alleged unauthorised spectrum use?
stories.why: Singapore's fourth telco is under regulatory scrutiny, and its customers' numbers and service could be caught in the middle.

stories.summary: Singapore remains South-east Asia's leading headquarters hub despite rising costs, with the number of companies setting up regional headquarters here passing 1,000.
stories.title: Is Singapore still South-east Asia's headquarters haven?
stories.why: A vote of confidence in Singapore's hub status even as costs climb — and a counterweight to the gloom in regional markets.

stories.summary: DBS, OCBC and UOB see strong demand to finance AI data centres across South-east Asia but are staying highly selective, favouring strong sponsors and cash flows amid debt-risk concerns.
stories.title: Singapore banks stay selective on AI data centre financing
stories.why: Singapore's banks are gatekeepers to the region's AI build-out — and their caution says something about how frothy that boom looks from the inside.

stories.summary: After the Fed's September rate hike, Singapore banks have pulled and repriced fixed-rate mortgage packages — up 0.30–0.77 percentage points — and today's packages suggest rates may hold or rise only mildly, with the lowest two-year fixed rate at 1.5%.
stories.title: Could mortgage rates rise further? What bank packages in Singapore are signalling after Fed hike
stories.why: The first read on where home-loan rates go next — and a signal that the post-hike repricing may be mostly done.

stories.summary: A federal investigation is examining Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's alleged affair with Alice Huang, an executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed suspected of being recruited by Chinese intelligence; Nvidia says he never shared confidential information, and analysts have flagged succession risk at the world's most valuable chipmaker.
stories.title: Jensen Huang: What we know about Nvidia CEO's affair with suspected Chinese spy
stories.why: The probe now reaches the top of the AI industry — and Singapore sits at the centre of the chip-smuggling scrutiny.

stories.summary: AMD shares jumped 13% after a multi-year AI chip deal with Google Cloud, leading a broad tech rally that also lifted Micron 6% as chip stocks recovered from last week's rout.
stories.title: Advanced Micro Devices soars 13% on Google Cloud deal, tech rally
stories.why: The first sign the AI sell-off may be turning — and a reminder that the rally is spreading beyond Nvidia.

stories.summary: The EU has sued IBM, French IT group Atos and Italian defence contractor Leonardo over repeated delays in building its new smart border Entry/Exit System, the Financial Times reported; the system, which electronically records non-EU nationals' entries and exits across Schengen, is running but the dispute covers delays during development.
stories.title: EU sues IBM, two others over border system delays
stories.why: Brussels is taking its own border-tech contractors to court — a rare public fight over one of Europe's biggest IT projects.

stories.summary: UK retailers are using live facial-recognition technology to identify known shoplifters as they enter stores, in a BBC report examining how the systems work and the privacy debate around them.
stories.title: The facial recognition technology stopping shoplifters
stories.why: Live facial recognition is moving from airports and policing into the high street — and the privacy rules haven't caught up.

stories.summary: MARTAC delivered two Devil Ray T38 uncrewed surface vessels to the Philippine Navy — its first in South-east Asia — for coastal security and surveillance missions.
stories.title: MARTAC Delivers Two Devil Ray T38 USVs To Philippine Navy
stories.why: Uncrewed naval systems are arriving in South-east Asian waters, starting with the Philippines' coastal patrols.

stories.summary: Wall Street rallied overnight while Nvidia sank on the spy probe into its CEO, the ASX jumped in early trade, and oil fell on hopes of a US–Iran deal.
stories.title: Markets today: Wall Street rallies, Nvidia sinks amid spy probe; ASX jumps in early trade
stories.why: Markets are rallying into the week's big test — US CPI lands tonight — with the Nvidia probe as the main drag.

stories.summary: Colombia's state oil company Ecopetrol launched a $2 billion dollar-bond sale — its first since 2022 — to refinance debt.
stories.title: Ecopetrol Offers Dollar Bonds for First Time Since 2022 to Refinance Debt
stories.why: A big emerging-market borrower testing appetite for dollar debt as the Fed's path stays uncertain.

stories.summary: Mexico approved a capital-markets modernisation introducing simplified listing rules, aiming to attract more listings and investment in 2027.
stories.title: Mexico Modernizes Capital Markets for 2027
stories.why: Latin America's second-largest economy is trying to revive a thin stock market — a test case for EM reform.

stories.summary: Singapore semiconductor stock AEM Holdings has been hit hard in the AI sell-off, down about 45% in the past month, but CGS International kept its Add call while cutting its target price to S$12.92; its third-quarter results are due tomorrow.
stories.title: AEM: Caught in AI Selloff, CGS Keeps Bullish Call Despite Lower Target
stories.why: The AI rout is hitting Singapore's chip supply chain directly — and tomorrow's results are the next test.

stories.summary: Republican Representative Thomas Massie filed a resolution to impeach US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth, accusing him of illegally waging war without congressional authorisation and of ordering strikes on boats the US claimed were smuggling drugs; the House could vote as early as Wednesday.
stories.title: US congressman files resolution to impeach Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth
stories.why: The Iran war's political fallout has reached the Pentagon's top job — filed by a Republican, with a floor vote possible this week.

stories.summary: President Trump said on Monday the war in Iran 'militarily is effectively over' and signalled no immediate return to strikes, while keeping forces ready — saying the US has identified targets including 38 bridges if military action resumes.
stories.title: Iran war: Trump says conflict is 'effectively over', signals no immediate strikes
stories.why: The clearest signal yet that the Iran war is winding down rather than restarting — after the midterms.

stories.summary: Pakistan condemned a Houthi attack targeting a Saudi Aramco administrative building in Riyadh, after Saudi air defences intercepted two ballistic missiles and falling shrapnel caused minor damage; the Houthis have stepped up attacks on Saudi airports, ports and energy facilities.
stories.title: Pakistan slams Houthi attack on Saudi Aramco tower, demands immediate halt to strikes
stories.why: The Yemen conflict is spilling back into Saudi cities — and drawing in Pakistan, a signatory of the new Saudi defence pact.

stories.summary: Canadian armoured-vehicle maker Roshel will buy Stellantis's Brampton assembly plant to expand production, as demand for military vehicles grows.
stories.title: Roshel to buy Stellantis assembly plant in Brampton for undisclosed amount, automaker says
stories.why: Defence demand is now reshaping car plants — an automaker's factory becomes an armoured-vehicle line.

stories.summary: Bangladesh formed a panel to develop its defence industry, aiming to boost local production and cut dependence on imports.
stories.title: Panel formed to develop defence industry
stories.why: Another Asian state moves to build its own arms industry rather than buy abroad.

stories.summary: A covert Russian disinformation network known as Operation Overload exploited France's October protests, spreading fabricated videos impersonating Western news outlets — falsely claiming migrants had raped protesters or that terrorist attacks were imminent — according to an internal EU assessment seen by Reuters; investigators found no evidence Russia organised the protests themselves.
stories.title: Russian Disinformation Exploited French Protests to Undermine Macron
stories.why: A case study in how foreign networks hijack a real domestic crisis — and how impersonated journalism is now the delivery method.

stories.summary: Australia's Human Rights Commission warned in a new report, 'Breaking Trust', that synthetic media is becoming a low-cost, scalable tool for manipulating public debate — used to discredit candidates, mislead voters and target women and minorities — and called for urgent action on deepfake risks.
stories.title: Australia must act now on growing risks from deepfakes
stories.why: A national human rights body putting synthetic media on the same footing as other threats to democracy — ahead of Australia's own election cycle pressures.

tldr: Marsiling's wartime fuel tunnels get a heritage study, IMDA's probe into Simba puts customers' numbers in question, and banks stay picky on AI data-centre loans while mortgage rates edge up.
Nvidia's CEO spy-affair probe deepens with a federal investigation, AMD jumps 13% on a Google Cloud AI chip deal, and the EU sues IBM, Atos and Leonardo over its delayed smart-border system.

Wall Street rallied as Nvidia sank on the spy probe, Ecopetrol returned to the dollar bond market with $2bn, Mexico overhauled its capital markets, and Singapore's AEM stays caught in the AI sell-off.
A Republican filed to impeach Pentagon chief Hegseth, Trump declared the Iran war 'effectively over', and Houthi strikes hit an Aramco building in Riyadh.
A Russian network exploited France's October riots with fake news, an EU assessment found, and Australia's human rights watchdog warned deepfakes are eroding trust in democracy.
